title: Subnet News — October 15, 2026
summary: SN96 Verathos Decide launches with operational model endpoints, SN92 REAX identifies its decision-inference network, and SN75 Hippius launches Projects. SN28 SayGM adds video generation, SN65 TPN opens its next competition, and SN105 Beam pilots customer discovery with SN71 Leadpoet. Also: SN38 ChronoLLM’s roadmap, active runtime 479, miner fixes, unresolved incidents and the SN48 Quantum Compute replay. Coverage through October 15 at 10:31 AM Eastern; SN80 OpenRoboto’s peaq fleet integration is also confirmed.

updates.headline: SN1 Apex and Bitstarter schedule an Accelerator reveal
updates.summary: SN1 Apex and Bitstarter describe testing incentive mechanisms with SN1 Apex miners before teams launch their own subnet, with a fuller reveal on October 16. The harness is presented as reducing competition creation from weeks to minutes; that claim was not independently timed. This is a counterpart-confirmed partnership and upcoming reveal, not proof participants have registered subnets or secured customers.
updates.ratingReason: Plans offer teams a concrete way to test incentives before launch.

sources.label: SN1 Apex original Accelerator post
Bitstarter counterpart reveal

updates.headline: SN7 allways adds USDC routes in code and reports fee coverage
updates.summary: SN7 allways code adds Avalanche and HyperEVM USDC launch spokes. Its public October 14 post lists five previously available destinations; the new code is not end-to-end confirmation of both added routes. The October 15 digest attributes $2,569.95 of fees across 349 transactions to the team, described as 159% of estimated miner emissions. These are unaudited period-specific figures, not net profit after every expense or future coverage guarantees.
updates.ratingReason: Route implementation and attributed usage economics advance the service beyond market chatter.

updates.headline: SN8 Vanta updates Classic rules and Instant sizes
updates.summary: SN8 Vanta’s October 14 published rules raise Classic portfolio buying power to 40×, with asset-class caps including 30× forex and 10× crypto. The October 15 post expands Instant Funded to $25k,$50k and $100k sizes. These are simulated-account rules, not cash in a brokerage account. A separate post advertises a $100,111.47 largest USDC reward, but the readable ledger repeats it in a snapshot labelled September 23; it is not treated as a newly executed October 14 payout, and its transaction was not independently verified. The older listing teaser still lacks venue/date confirmation.
updates.ratingReason: Concrete product/rule changes are reported with simulated-capital and payout-date distinctions.

updates.headline: SN10 Pareton stops closed campaigns spawning rounds
updates.summary: SN10 Pareton now checks open status when queuing, creating and claiming rounds. Previously closing stopped weights but could leave rounds voiding on hardware mismatch and requeueing challengers. Queued work remains available for reopening. Another correction charges short completions at full length in timing. These improve campaign integrity, not a new inference-speed result.
updates.ratingReason: Primary fixes prevent invalid continued work and misleading timing.

updates.headline: SN15 ORO separates exhausted credits from environment faults
updates.summary: SN15 ORO now treats an OpenRouter 402 insufficient-credit reply as an exhausted miner run key. Runtime 3.7.1 also makes the shared task catalog thread-safe, fixing concurrent cache eviction. This distinguishes funding exhaustion from environment failure and reduces spurious failed runs. It does not establish that every anti-cheat rejection was wrong or every race is error-free.
updates.ratingReason: Primary fixes separate concrete failure sources affecting miner runs.

updates.headline: SN18 Zeus changes reward ranking to win rate
updates.summary: SN18 Zeus’ merged reward function uses win rate over the window instead of mean rank. This changes the performance signal miners compete on, distinct from posting a conference talk. A merge does not establish adoption by every validator or a new forecast-accuracy result.
updates.ratingReason: A primary metric change can alter rankings and incentives.

updates.headline: SN28 SayGM adds text-to-video and image-to-video creation
updates.summary: SN28 SayGM’s October 14 thread announces MiniMax H3 video creation, naming SN90 KubeTEE as its provider. Users start with a prompt, one image or start/end frames to create a clip with sound. Public gateway documentation also describes asynchronous jobs, polling and MP4 output. This expands the product beyond text and still images. Demonstrations are team examples, not a quality benchmark or a guarantee of generation time. The provider relationship is attributed to the thread; a separate counterpart announcement was not obtained.

updates.headline: SN30 Endure publishes a five-round forecast check
updates.summary: SN30 Endure reports 62 of 75 forecasts across October 4–8 were at least as large as the subsequent worst five-day drop for 15 subnets. Thirteen underestimated the drop; many others substantially overestimated it. This distinguishes coverage from calibration:62/75 is not an 82.7% exact-price prediction rate. The linked dashboard reports partial indexing, and the underlying round history was not independently reproduced.
updates.ratingReason: A dated outcome comparison exposes forecast limitations rather than equating conservative coverage with exact accuracy.

updates.summary: SN38 ChronoLLM’s October 14 article says Round 16 uses vintage 2025, then Round 17 begins walking backward from 2012 toward 1999, one year per round. This raises the difficulty of sourcing contemporaneous data without later knowledge leaking into training. Its first public customer product is targeted for the first week of November, with use-case contributors invited. These are planned steps, not a product already launched. The article does not adjudicate the prior Round 15 dispute.

updates.headline: SN50 Synth fixes look-ahead contamination in backtests
updates.summary: SN50 Synth’s Campaign 4 patch stops a scored prompt taking a prediction that starts after it, when context could already contain part of the realized price path. Matching now looks backward within a tolerance. Other repairs use close rather than open prices and respect read-only snapshot cutoffs. This matters because a forecast must not benefit from future information. The failure class is documented; every past score and any historical ranking recalculation were not independently reconstructed.
updates.ratingReason: A primary patch addresses concrete look-ahead bias that can materially distort evaluation.

sources.label: SN50 primary implementation and release notes

updates.headline: SN56 Gradients changes training-overhead bands
updates.summary: SN56 Gradients replaces flat 0.75 hour overhead and lowers the task-duration minimum to 0.25 hours. A subsequent correction sets smaller-model overhead to 0.4 hours below 1B and 0.6 hours for 1–4B, retaining 0.75 hours for larger models. The intermediate first-commit values are not today’s final code. This fits scheduling to model size; it is not a measured training-speed gain.
updates.ratingReason: Specific scheduling parameters affect task sizing and expected GPU utilization.

updates.headline: SN65 TPN opens TPN-006 with an 8 GiB target
updates.summary: SN65 TPN’s October 15 announcement opens TPN-006, asking miners to shrink Ministral-3-8B Uncensored to an 8 GiB ceiling while retaining 32k context, versus the previous 11 GiB ceiling. The announced King-of-the-Hill winner receives the full 25% emission weight assigned to this competition, scored on fluid_knowledge. This is a new optimization target, not an already successful 8 GiB model or 25% of all Bittensor emissions. Yesterday’s TPN-005 evidence remains the earlier result.
updates.ratingReason: A new competition changes the memory constraint and gives miners a fresh objective.

updates.headline: SN75 Hippius launches Projects
updates.summary: SN75 Hippius’ October 15 announcement introduces separate client, team or environment spaces with their own VMs, S3 buckets/keys, CDN zones, billing wallets and invoices. It describes project-scoped access, daily costs, budget alerts and an optional block on new launches at the limit. Existing resources sit in a Default project. This makes managing multiple customers or environments more practical. The announced no-downtime project-transfer flow was not exercised in this read-only review.

updates.headline: SN80 OpenRoboto’s peaq integration gets confirmation from Solana
updates.summary: SN80 OpenRoboto’s October 15 thread says its first 30 OR-S1 data collectors now use peaqOS Pro, each with a decentralized identity anchored on Solana. peaq’s counterpart post confirms 30 live units and says future collectors will follow. This advances yesterday’s scheduled discussion/teaser to a specifically announced fleet integration, giving buyers a checkable device identity behind captured robotics data. It does not by itself prove every recording is authentic or independently validate the hardware. Connecting the fleet to machine money markets is described as the next step, not financing already received. The October 19 discussion remains a separate upcoming event. Update: Solana’s official account also highlighted the integration on October 15 at 15:33 UTC (11:33 AM Eastern), saying the devices have Solana identities and wallets and can be verified and paid for performance through peaq. This adds acknowledgement from the chain’s own account and explains the payment capability; it is not evidence that a specific payment or financing transaction has already occurred.
updates.ratingReason: Both sides confirm a specific deployed fleet integration rather than only a partnership teaser.

sources.label: SN80 OpenRoboto original 30-collector announcement

updates.headline: SN92 REAX identifies its network; competitions are planned for October 16
updates.summary: The current SN92 name is REAX, and reax.co and its public repository explicitly identify netuid 92. The project hosts pinned decision models, checking fidelity before adding a speed component to scoring. Decisionmodels.io is its customer-facing API. The site labels inference live and schedules competitions for October 16 at 12:00 UTC; those competitions are still upcoming. Hardware tiers and shares differ across release documents, so the digest’s 80/20 claim is not treated as a verified finalized allocation. Customer volume and GDPR compliance were not independently audited. This identifies a project on an existing slot, not a fresh registration or sale. Const’s ownership denial remains context. The alpha/TAO snapshot shows +109.42% over 24 hours without attributing the move to one announcement.
updates.ratingReason: Official site/repository linkage resolves the previously unknown identity and provides a concrete product and schedule.

ecosystem.headline: Finney runtime 479 is active
ecosystem.summary: Our finalized node returns specVersion 479 at block 9,289,273, advancing yesterday’s 478. Its merged release includes an opt-out from third-party additions to a coldkey’s staking-hotkey list, with contract checks and a dedicated refusal error. It also documents rejecting EIP-7702 authorization lists above 255 entries before signature recovery. These are account/resource safeguards. The previously reduced immunity and registration-cost decay values are unchanged; this is not another halving of those limits.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Direct runtime evidence and primary code establish active account and resource safeguards.
